title: econ-signal-and-batch-default-prober
author: Aisha Kaur
release_notes: Added an 'econ signal' service that synthesizes per-route unit cost estimates and a 'batch-default-prober' tool to auto-suggest batching/caching/quant profiles. New CLI: 'redwood econ preview'. Non-breaking; opt-in via config.
description:
Motivation: customers frequently ask for straightforward defaults that balance latency and unit economics for new routes. Existing autotuners require long collection windows or manual profiling. This PR introduces two pieces: (1) an econ-signal microservice that ingests a small replay and emits per-route unit-econ signals (token cost, effective throughput, headroom) and (2) a batch-default-prober that runs fast microbenchmarks against candidate batching/cache/quant profiles and returns ranked recommendations. Together they allow engineers to get cost-aware defaults within minutes rather than days.

What this changes (high-level):
- runtime/service: new package redwood/econ-signal that implements a light-weight sampler, cost model, and signal exporter. It integrates with existing telemetry and exposes a small HTTP gRPC-compatible API used by CLI and Console.
- tooling/cli: added redwood econ preview --workload <replay.tar.gz> --route <route-id> that runs the prober locally or in-cluster and prints a ranked table of recommended profiles (batch_size, prefill_kv_cache, quant_profile, expected tokens/sec, estimated $/1M tokens).
- profiles: baked a new set of quantization profile templates (q4_fast_latency, q4_cost_saver, int8_safe) and prefill presets for small/medium/large request shapes.
- telemetry: instrumented events econ.prober.run, econ.signal.estimate, econ.recommendation.choice; added a few labels for workload_shape and route_tier to aid later A/B.
- docs: new quickstart in docs/econ/quickstart.md and CLI man page.
- tests: unit tests for the cost model, end-to-end integration test that runs the prober with a synthetic replay on a small local runtime.

performance_results: Local prober microbenchmarks (2x A100) show recommended batch default (batch=8, prefill=enabled, quant=q4_cost_saver) yields median token latency +8% and cost per token -32% compared to baseline (no batching, fp16). For small interactive routes our heuristics prefer prefill=false and smaller batches; for throughput routes recommended configs reduced $/1M tokens by 28-39% in synthetic replays.
rollout_notes: Opt-in default: new econ-signal service is disabled by default in hosted and dedicated. Console will surface a 'Try recommended defaults' affordance after deployment. Admins can enable automated suggestion application via feature flag feature.econ.apply_recommendations in config. Monitoring: watch econ.prober.run counts, econ.recommendation.choice distribution, and latency.p95 per route. Rollback: flip feature flag or disable service; suggestions are non-destructive until manually applied.
